Benchmark.title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
Benchmark.description: All CIS Benchmarks ™ (Benchmarks) focus on technical configuration settings used to maintain and/or increase the security of the addressed technology, and they should be used in conjunction with other essential cyber hygiene tasks like: • Monitoring the base operating system and applications for vulnerabilities and quickly updating with the latest security patches. • End-point protection (Antivirus software, Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), etc.). • Logging and monitoring user and system activity. In the end, the Benchmarks are designed to be a key component of a comprehensive cybersecurity program. Important Usage Information All Benchmarks are available free for non-commercial use from the CIS Website. They can be used to manually assess and remediate systems and applications. In lieu of manual assessment and remediation, there are several tools available to assist with assessment: • CIS Configuration Assessment Tool (CIS-CAT ® Pro Assessor) • CIS Benchmarks ™ Certified 3rd Party Tooling These tools make the hardening process much more scalable for large numbers of systems and applications. NOTE: Some tooling focuses only on the Benchmark Recommendations that can be fully automated (skipping ones marked Manual). It is important that ALL Recommendations ( Automated and Manual) be addressed since all are important for properly securing systems and are typically in scope for audits. Key Stakeholders Cybersecurity is a collaborative effort, and cross functional cooperation is imperative within an organization to discuss, test, and deploy Benchmarks in an effective and efficient way. The Benchmarks are developed to be best practice configuration guidelines applicable to a wide range of use cases. In some organizations, exceptions to specific Recommendations will be needed, and this team should work to prioritize the problematic Recommendations based on several factors like risk, time, cost, and labor. These exceptions should be properly categorized and documented for auditing purposes. Apply the Correct Version of a Benchmark Benchmarks are developed and tested for a specific set of products and versions and applying an incorrect Benchmark to a system can cause the resulting pass/fail score to be incorrect. This is due to the assessment of settings that do not apply to the target systems. To assure the correct Benchmark is being assessed: • Deploy the Benchmark applicable to the way settings are managed in the environment: An example of this is the Microsoft Windows family of Benchmarks, which have separate Benchmarks for Group Policy, Intune, and Stand-alone systems based upon how system management is deployed. Applying the wrong Benchmark in this case will give invalid results. • Use the most recent version of a Benchmark: This is true for all Benchmarks, but especially true for cloud technologies. Cloud technologies change frequently and using an older version of a Benchmark may have invalid methods for auditing and remediation. Exceptions The guidance items in the Benchmarks are called recommendations and not requirements, and exceptions to some of them are expected and acceptable. The Benchmarks strive to be a secure baseline, or starting point, for a specific technology, with known issues identified during Benchmark development are documented in the Impact section of each Recommendation. In addition, organizational, system specific requirements, or local site policy may require changes as well, or an exception to a Recommendation or group of Recommendations (e.g. A Benchmark could Recommend that a Web server not be installed on the system, but if a system's primary purpose is to function as a Webserver, there should be a documented exception to this Recommendation for that specific server). In the end, exceptions to some Benchmark Recommendations are common and acceptable, and should be handled as follows: • The reasons for the exception should be reviewed cross-functionally and be well documented for audit purposes. • A plan should be developed for mitigating, or eliminating, the exception in the future, if applicable. • If the organization decides to accept the risk of this exception (not work toward mitigation or elimination), this should be documented for audit purposes. It is the responsibility of the organization to determine their overall security policy, and which settings are applicable to their unique needs based on the overall risk profile for the organization. Remediation CIS has developed Build Kits for many technologies to assist in the automation of hardening systems. Build Kits are designed to correspond to Benchmark's “Remediation” section, which provides the manual remediation steps necessary to make that Recommendation compliant to the Benchmark. When remediating systems (changing configuration settings on deployed systems as per the Benchmark's Recommendations), please approach this with caution and test thoroughly. The following is a reasonable remediation approach to follow: • CIS Build Kits, or internally developed remediation methods should never be applied to production systems without proper testing. • Proper testing consists of the following: o Understand the configuration (including installed applications) of the targeted systems. Various parts of the organization may need different configurations (e.g., software developers vs standard office workers). o Read the Impact section of the given Recommendation to help determine if there might be an issue with the targeted systems. o Test the configuration changes with representative lab system(s). If issues arise during testing, they can be resolved prior to deploying to any production systems. o When testing is complete, initially deploy to a small sub-set of production systems and monitor closely for issues. If there are issues, they can be resolved prior to deploying more broadly. o When the initial deployment above is completed successfully, iteratively deploy to additional systems and monitor closely for issues. Repeat this process until the full deployment is complete. Summary Using the Benchmarks Certified tools, working as a team with key stakeholders, being selective with exceptions, and being careful with remediation deployment, it is possible to harden large numbers of deployed systems in a cost effective, efficient, and safe manner. NOTE: As previously stated, the PDF versions of the CIS Benchmarks ™ are available for free, non-commercial use on the CIS Website. All other formats of the CIS Benchmarks ™ (MS Word, Excel, and Build Kits) are available for CIS SecureSuite ® members. CIS-CAT ® Pro is also available to CIS SecureSuite ® members. Target Technology Details This document, CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark, provides prescriptive guidance for establishing a secure configuration posture for OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4. This guide was tested against OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 running on Ubuntu Linux, but applies to other Linux distributions as well. To obtain the latest version of this guide, please visit http://benchmarks.cisecurity.org. If you have questions, comments, or have identified ways to improve this guide, please write us at feedback@cisecurity.org.

Rule.title: Place Databases on Non-System Partitions
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>It is generally accepted that host operating systems should include different filesystem partitions for different purposes. One set of filesystems is typically called system partitions, and these are generally reserved for host system/application operation. The other set of filesystems is typically called "non-system partitions", and such locations are generally reserved for storing data.
Rationale: Moving the database off the system partition will reduce the probability of denial of service caused by exhaustion of available disk space to the operating system.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.fixtext: Perform the following steps to remediate this setting for the datadir: 1. Backup the database. 2. Choose a non-system partition new location for OceanBase data files. 3. Stop observer using a command like: pkill -9 observer. 4. Copy the data using a command like: cp -rp <datadir> <new location>. 5. Delete datadir and create a symlink instead to point to the new location using a command like: ln -s <new location> <datadir> 6. Restart observer.

check.check-content: Use the following procedure to assess compliance: 1. Connect to the OceanBase database as an administrative user and run: SELECT svr_ip, name, value FROM oceanbase.GV$OB_PARAMETERS WHERE name = 'data_dir'; 2. For each returned value (e.g., /data/1), determine its filesystem mount point by running: df -h <datadir>/sstable 3. Examine the "Mounted on" column in the output. This recommendation is compliant if the filesystem mounted at the OceanBase data_dir path (and any associated subdirectories such as log or sstable directories) is not the root ( /), /var, or /usr filesystem. Repeat this check for other critical OceanBase directories if they are configured separately, such as <datadir>/clog 、 <datadir>/slog.

Rule.title: Ensure the Partition Size for Log Files is Large Enough
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>The database files and directories should place to a non-system partition and the partition size should be large enough. For OceanBase stable running and accommondating log growth, the partition size for OceanBase log files must have at least 3-4 times the available memory .
Rationale: Designating enough partition size for OceanBase log files will accommodate log growth, prevent performance bottlenecks and reduce the probability of denial of service caused by exhaustion of available disk space.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.fixtext: Assume the disk used for the log partition is large enough. Then perform the following steps to remediate this setting for the log directory: 1. Backup the database. 2. Stop observer using a command like: pkill -9 observer. 3. Dismount the log partition usming command like: umount /data/log1. 4. Resize the log partition and the filesystem. 5. Mount the log partition to the original directory: mount <partition> /data/log1. 6. Restart observer. 7. Connect to the OceanBase database as an administrative user and increase the log_disk_size parameter to satisfy the 3-4 times memory requirement. For example, if the observer's available memory is 20G and the new partition size is sufficient (e.g., > 60G), set the log_disk_size to 60G (3 times the memory). ALTER SYSTEM SET log_disk_size = '60G';

check.check-content: Use the following procedure to assess compliance: 1. Connect to the OceanBase database as an administrative user and retrieve the data directory: SELECT svr_ip, name, value FROM oceanbase.GV$OB_PARAMETERS WHERE name = 'data_dir'; 2. Determine the observer’s available memory: • Run: SELECT svr_ip,name,value FROM oceanbase.GV$OB_PARAMETERS WHERE name like 'memory_limit%'; • If memory_limit is not zero, use its value (in bytes). • If memory_limit is zero, calculate available memory as: available_memory = memory_limit_percentage × total_system_memory Obtain total_system_memory from the OS: grep MemTotal /proc/meminfo 3. For each log directory path (e.g., /data/log1), run: df -h /data/log1 This recommendation is satisfied if the total size of the filesystem hosting the OceanBase log directories is at least three to four times the observer’s configured available memory. If the log partition size is less than this threshold, the system is non- compliant.

Rule.title: Ensure 'data_dir' Has Appropriate Permissions
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>The cluster-level configuration parameter 'data_dir' displays the directory for storing data such as SSTables. Currently, it is read-only and cannot be modified.
Rationale: Restricting access permissions to this directory helps protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the OceanBase database.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.fixtext: To remediate incorrect permissions or ownership on the OceanBase data directory: 1. Confirm the current permissions and ownership: ls -ld /data/1 2. Set the correct ownership to the admin user and group: sudo chown admin:admin /data/1 3. Restrict permissions to owner read/write/execute and group read/execute only: sudo chmod 750 /data/1 4. Verify the change: ls -ld /data/1 Expected output: drwxr-x--- 10 admin admin 4096 Jan 1 10:00 /data/1

check.check-content: Use the following procedure to assess compliance: 1. Connect to the OceanBase database as an administrative user and retrieve the data directory path: SELECT svr_ip,name,value FROM oceanbase.GV$OB_PARAMETERS WHERE name='data_dir'; Example output: /data/1 or./store. 2. On the host system, inspect the permissions and ownership of the returned path: ls -ld /data/1 Note: If the path is a symbolic link, use ls -ldL /data/1 to examine the target directory’s attributes. This recommendation is satisfied if the directory has permissions set to 750 (i.e., drwxr-x---) and is owned by the admin user and admin group. Any deviation — such as world-readable permissions ( o+r), group-write access ( g+w), or incorrect ownership — constitutes non-compliance.

Rule.title: Use Dedicated Least Privileged Account for OceanBase Daemon/Service
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>As with any service installed on a host, it can be provided with its own user context. Providing a dedicated user to the service provides the ability to precisely constrain the service within the larger host context.
Rationale: Utilizing a least privilege account for OceanBase to execute as needed may reduce the impact of a OceanBase-born vulnerability. A restricted account will be unable to access resources unrelated to OceanBase, such as operating system configurations.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.fixtext: To ensure OceanBase runs under a dedicated service account: 1. Create a dedicated user (skip this step if using the default admin user, provided it is not shared): sudo useradd -r /sbin/nologin -c "OceanBase Service Account" obuser 2. Identify all OceanBase-related paths, including: • Installation directory (e.g., /home/admin/oceanbase) • Data directory (data_dir, e.g., /data/1) • Log directories (e.g., /data/log1) 3. Stop observer using a command like: pkill -9 observer. 4. Copy the OceanBase installation directory to the dedicated user's home directory: sudo cp -a /home/admin/oceanbase /home/obuser/ 5. Change ownership of all relevant directories to the dedicated user: sudo chown -R obuser:obuser /data/1 /data/log1 /home/obuser/oceanbase 6. Restart observer. 7. Verify: ps -eo user,comm | grep observer Confirm the process runs as obuser (or admin) and not root. 8. Test database connectivity and basic operations to ensure functionality is unaffected.

check.check-content: Use the following procedure to assess compliance: 1. Identify the user under which the OceanBase observer process is running: ps -eo pid,user,comm | grep observer Example compliant output: 12345 admin observer 2. Verify that the user is: • Not root • A dedicated service account (e.g., admin, obuser, or similar), not a shared or interactive user account. This recommendation is satisfied if the observer process runs under a non-root, dedicated user account created specifically for OceanBase. The system is non- compliant if the process runs as root or under a general-purpose user account (e.g., ubuntu, ec2-user).

Rule.title: Ensure the Appropriate Version for OceanBase Software Is Installed
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>The OceanBase installation version should be the most recent that are compatible with the organization's operational needs.
Rationale: Using the most recent OceanBase database software can help limit the possibilities for vulnerabilities in the software, the installation version applied during setup should be established according to the needs of the organization. Ensure you are using a release that is covered by a level of support that includes the generation of critical patches.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.fixtext: Perform the following steps for remediation: 1. Identify the target version: • Check the Release Notes to find the latest LTS (Long Term Support) version or the latest compatible patch version. 2. Download and apply the upgrade: • Download the installation package for the target version. • Upgrade the observer using the OceanBase Control Platform (OCP) or your standard upgrade procedure.

check.check-content: Use the following procedure to assess compliance: 1. Retrieve the currently running OceanBase version: SELECT ob_version(); Example output: 4.2.1.0 2. Consult the OceanBase Product Lifecycle documentation to verify the support status: • Link: OceanBase Product Lifecycle • Check: Ensure the current date is before the EOS (End of Standard Support) or EOES (End of Extended Support) date for your version. • Identify: Check if your version is marked as LTS (Long Term Support), which is recommended for production environments. 3. This recommendation is satisfied if the running version is active (not EOL) and preferably an LTS version.

Rule.title: Use OceanBase Official Signed Installation Packages
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>OceanBase official release packages are signed with a GPG key. Before using the packages, users can verify their integrity by checking the signature, thereby preventing supply chain poisoning attacks caused by tampered or untrusted installation packages.
Rationale: Ensuring the integrity and authenticity of installation packages during software distribution is a core security measure to defend against supply chain attacks. GPG signatures, based on asymmetric encryption technology, provide a digital fingerprint for software packages, ensuring they have not been altered since signing and verifying the identity of the publisher.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.fixtext: Ensure that all OceanBase installation packages used in production environments are obtained directly from official OceanBase distribution channels and bear valid digital signatures issued by OceanBase. Coordinate with authorized OceanBase support or delivery personnel to confirm the authenticity and integrity of software packages prior to deployment. Under no circumstances should unsigned, modified, or third-party redistributed packages be deployed in production systems.

check.check-content: For environments deployed using the OceanBase Cloud Platform (OCP), verify that installation packages are sourced exclusively from official OceanBase channels and that OCP’s built -in signature validation mechanism is enabled. Review deployment logs or audit records from OCP to confirm that no unsigned or untrusted packages were installed. The presence of alerts or rejection events related to package signature validation indicates that the control is active. This recommendation is satisfied if the organization can demonstrate, through deployment documentation or OCP audit trails, that only officially signed OceanBase packages have been used in production deployments.

Rule.title: Backup Strategy in Place
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>A backup strategy should be in place.
Rationale: Backing up OceanBase tenants will help to ensure the availability of data in the event of an incident. Without backups, it might be hard to recover from an incident.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.fixtext: Establish a formal backup strategy aligned with business continuity requirements: • Define backup scope (which tenants/databases), frequency, retention period, and storage location. • If using OCP, configure automated backup policies through the platform’s backup management interface. • If not using OCP, implement and document a repeatable backup procedure using supported OceanBase tools, and schedule it via cron or orchestration systems. • Regularly test backup restoration in a non-production environment to validate recoverability. Note: Backups should be stored securely, preferably on separate storage systems or offsite, to protect against site-wide failures.

check.check-content: Verify that a backup strategy exists and is actively configured for OceanBase tenants: • If OceanBase Cloud Platform (OCP) is used, review the backup policies and schedules configured in OCP for each production tenant. Confirm that backups are scheduled at an appropriate frequency (e.g., daily) and that recent successful backup jobs are recorded in the OCP job history. • If OCP is not deployed, examine organizational documentation (e.g., operations runbooks, disaster recovery plans) or database logs to confirm that manual or script-based backups (e.g., using obd tools) are performed regularly and verified. This recommendation is satisfied if the organization can demonstrate — through OCP configuration, backup logs, or documented procedures — that a consistent and recoverable backup process is in place for all critical OceanBase tenants.

Rule.title: Enable Automatic Major Compaction before Backup
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Automatic major compaction should be enabled before the backup is scheduled.
Rationale: If automatic major compaction is enabled, a major compaction will be automatically triggered during backup scheduling when the backup depends on a major compaction.If automatic major compaction is disabled, automatic major compaction will not be triggered during backup scheduling, and this may cause a backup scheduling failure.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.fixtext: Ensure that automatic major compaction is enabled for all tenants that are configured for backup: • When using OceanBase Cloud Platform (OCP), update the tenant’s backup policy to include automatic major compaction as a prerequisite step. • In environments managed without OCP, work with database administrators to configure the system to trigger major compaction automatically prior to backup execution, in accordance with OceanBase best practices. • Document this configuration in the organization’s operational procedures and validate that subsequent backup jobs complete successfully.

check.check-content: Review the backup configuration for each OceanBase tenant to confirm that automatic major compaction is enabled as part of the backup policy: • If the OceanBase Cloud Platform (OCP) is used, examine the tenant-level backup settings within OCP and verify that the option to enable automatic major compaction (or equivalent setting related to compaction triggering during backup) is activated. • If OCP is not used, consult the organization’s deployment documentation, change records, or operational runbooks to confirm that automatic major compaction has been explicitly enabled for all tenants included in backup schedules. This recommendation is satisfied if there is documented evidence — through OCP configuration, operational procedures, or change management records — that automatic major compaction is enabled for all tenants subject to scheduled backups.

Rule.title: Configure Alert Threshold for Unexpected Backup Events
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>An alert should be triggered when the unexpected backup events occur such as data backup timeout, log backup delay or no successful data backup in many days.
Rationale: Alerts for unexpected events can enable timely detection of potential failure events, preventing data loss of backup data due to undetected errors.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.fixtext: Configure or adjust backup alert thresholds to ensure timely notification of failures: • In OceanBase Cloud Platform (OCP), update the tenant’s backup strategy to define appropriate alert thresholds based on observed backup behavior and business requirements. o For Data Backup Timeout, set the threshold to a value greater than the typical completion time of recent successful backups (e.g., 1.5× average duration). o For Log Backup Delay, consider log generation rate and network/storage performance when setting the threshold. o For Consecutive Days Without Successful Backup, ensure the alert period is no longer than the backup scheduling interval (e.g., if backups run daily, the alert should trigger within 1 – 2 days of failure). • Document the rationale for selected thresholds in operational runbooks or change records. • Validate that alerts are delivered to the appropriate monitoring or incident management system.

check.check-content: Review the backup alert configuration for each OceanBase tenant to confirm that meaningful thresholds are defined and aligned with organizational requirements: • If OceanBase Cloud Platform (OCP) is used, examine the tenant-level backup policy settings and verify that alert thresholds are configured for the following conditions: o Data backup timeout o Log backup delay o Consecutive days without a successful data backup • Confirm that the configured thresholds reflect the organization’s operational needs —for example, the “days without backup” threshold should not exceed the backup frequency, and timeout thresholds should account for typical backup durations under normal load. This recommendation is satisfied if OCP (or equivalent operational documentation) demonstrates that alert thresholds for backup anomalies are explicitly configured, non- default where necessary, and consistent with the organization’s data protection and incident response policies.

Rule.title: Point-in-Time Recovery
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>With clogs it is possible to implement point-in-time recovery. This makes it possible to restore the changes between the last full backup and the point-in-time. The clogs need to be backed up with data backup. The restore procedure should be created and tested.
Rationale: Using clogs can reduce the amount of information lost when recovering from a backup.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.fixtext: Enable clog backup and establish a recovery validation process: • In OceanBase Cloud Platform (OCP), modify the tenant’s backup policy to enable the Log Backup feature. Ensure the log backup destination is reliable and monitored. • Develop a formal point-in-time recovery procedure that outlines how to restore from a full backup and replay clogs to a specified timestamp. • Conduct periodic recovery drills (e.g., quarterly or annually) to validate that PITR works as expected and meets business continuity requirements. • Document the procedure, test results, and any lessons learned in the organization’s operational knowledge base.

check.check-content: Verify that clog (log) backup is enabled and that a restore procedure exists: • If OceanBase Cloud Platform (OCP) is used, review the tenant-level backup configuration and confirm that log backup is explicitly enabled as part of the backup strategy. • Additionally, examine operational documentation or disaster recovery plans to confirm that a point-in-time recovery procedure has been defined and tested within the past 12 months (or per organizational policy). This recommendation is satisfied if log backup is enabled for all critical tenants and there is documented evidence of a tested restore procedure that demonstrates successful point-in-time recovery using clog backups.

Rule.title: Verify Backups are Good
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Backups should be validated on a regular basis.
Rationale: Verifying that backups are occurring appropriately will help ensure data availability in the event of an incident. Without a well-tested backup, it might be hard to recover from an incident if the backup procedure contains errors or doesn't include all required data.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.fixtext: Establish a formal backup validation program: • Implement regular recovery sampling tasks via OceanBase Cloud Platform (OCP), scheduled at intervals aligned with business risk (e.g., quarterly for critical systems). • Ensure each test includes: o Restoration of a representative tenant or dataset; o Verification of data completeness and consistency; o Validation that applications can operate correctly on the restored data. • Document test results, including success/failure status, issues encountered, and remediation actions. • Retain validation records for audit and continuous improvement purposes.

check.check-content: Review evidence that backup validation is performed systematically: • Examine backup validation or recovery test reports from the past 12 months (or per organizational policy). These may include: o Test plans and execution records from OceanBase Control Platform (OCP) recovery sampling tasks; o Screenshots, logs, or audit trails showing successful restore operations; o Post-test summaries confirming data consistency and application functionality. • If OCP is used, confirm that recovery sampling tasks are configured and have executed successfully within the review period. This recommendation is satisfied if the organization maintains documented evidence of regular backup validation activities that demonstrate successful restoration of OceanBase tenant data using current backup sets.

Rule.title: Limit Accepted Transport Layer Security (TLS) Versions
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>OceanBase supports multiple protocols of TLS. The higher the version the stronger the security and/or better the performance.
Rationale: Requiring clients attempting to connect to OceanBase to use higher versions of TLS to better protect data in transit.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.fixtext: Set the system parameter to require TLSv1.2 or higher: ALTER SYSTEM SET sql_protocol_min_tls_version = 'TLSv1.2';

check.check-content: Determine the minimum TLS version enforced by the OceanBase server: 1. Execute the following SQL query as a user with system view access: SELECT svr_ip,name,value FROM oceanbase.GV$OB_PARAMETERS WHERE name='sql_protocol_min_tls_version'; 2. Review the returned value of the sql_protocol_min_tls_version parameter: • The configuration is compliant if the value is explicitly set to TLSv1.2, TLSv1.3, or a higher TLS version supported by the system. • The configuration is non-compliant if the value is TLSv1, TLSv1.1, or if the parameter is not configured (in which case the system permits connections using insecure legacy TLS versions by default). This recommendation is satisfied only if sql_protocol_min_tls_version is explicitly set to TLSv1.2 or higher on all observer nodes.

Rule.title: Only Approved Servers can Access
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Specify an allowlist of approved servers that can access to the cluster.
Rationale: When using cluster by specifying the allowlist explicitly, it can increase the security of the cluster as only servers in the allowlist are allowed to connect to the cluster.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.fixtext: Configure a restrictive allowlist of approved clients: 1. Identify all legitimate hosts that require SSL/TLS connectivity to the OceanBase cluster (e.g., application servers, OCP nodes, backup servers). 2. Set the parameter using the following SQL statement, replacing <approved_ips> with a comma-separated list of trusted IPs: ALTER SYSTEM SET _ob_ssl_invited_nodes='<ips_list_in_cluster>'; 3. Verify the change by re-running the audit query and confirming that only intended IPs are listed. 4. Test connectivity from approved and unapproved hosts to validate enforcement.

check.check-content: Execute the following SQL query to inspect the current SSL client allowlist configuration: SELECT svr_ip,name,value FROM oceanbase.GV$OB_PARAMETERS WHERE name='_ob_ssl_invited_nodes'; • The configuration is compliant if the value is explicitly set to a non-empty list of trusted IP addresses or hostnames (e.g., 192.168.1.10, 192.168.1.11). • The configuration is non-compliant if the value is set to 0.0.0.0/0, ALL, None, or effectively permits unrestricted access. This recommendation is satisfied only when _ob_ssl_invited_nodes is configured to a specific, limited set of authorized client or application server IPs.

Rule.title: Limit Accepted TLS Versions
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>OceanBase supports communication encryption to ensure that traffic between nodes cannot be eavesdropped or tampered with.
Rationale: Require clients attempting to connect to MySQL to use a higher version of TLS, to better protect data in transit. Disabling older versions known to have security vulnerabilities (such as TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1) can effectively prevent downgrade attacks and man-in-the-middle attacks, ensuring the confidentiality and integrity of communications.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.fixtext: Currently, OceanBase supports TLSv1.2 and TLSv1.3. After specifying the TLS version, if a connection uses SSL encryption, it will use the specified version or a higher supported version. Example setting the minimum version to TLSv1.2: ALTER SYSTEM SET sql_protocol_min_tls_version = 'TLSv1.2';

check.check-content: Execute the following command to view the current specified TLS version: SHOW PARAMETERS LIKE 'sql_protocol_min_tls_version'; This recommendation is satisfied if the returned value for sql_protocol_min_tls_versio n is set to TLSv1.2 or TLSv1.3 on all OBServer nodes. This recommendation is not satisfied if the returned value is none, any, TLSv1, or TLSv1.1, or if the value differs across OBServer nodes.

Rule.title: Ensure Replication Traffic is Secured
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>The replication traffic between servers in OceanBase cluster should be secured. Security measures should include ensuring the confidentiality and integrity of the traffic, and performing mutual authentication between the servers before performing replication.
Rationale: The replication traffic should be secured as it gives access to all transferred information and might leak passwords.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

check.check-content: Verify that mutual authentication and TLS are enforced for inter-node communication: 1. Confirm that mutual SSL authentication is required for clients (including other observer nodes): SELECT svr_ip,name,value FROM oceanbase.GV$OB_PARAMETERS WHERE name='ssl_client_authentication'; • Compliant if value = 'True'. • Non-compliant if value = 'False' or not set. 2. Confirm that the RPC authentication method enforces SSL-based identity verification: SELECT svr_ip,name,value FROM oceanbase.GV$OB_PARAMETERS WHERE name='rpc_server_authentication_method'; • Compliant if value = 'SSL_NO_ENCRYPT' and SSL certificates are properly deployed on all observer nodes. • Non-compliant if value = 'ALL' or any setting that permits unauthenticated or non-SSL connections. This recommendation is satisfied only when both parameters are correctly configured AND valid SSL certificates are installed on all observer nodes, enabling encrypted, mutually authenticated replication traffic.

Rule.title: Ensure Passwords are Set for All OceanBase Accounts
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>If any account exists without a password (i.e., a null-password account), it reduces the attack cost — attackers only need to guess the username correctly to gain access without requiring a password. Therefore, it is essential to ensure that all OceanBase accounts are configured with passwords to prevent unauthorized malicious users from accessing the database.
Rationale: Password is one of the core elements of authentication. If an account has no password, authentication is reduced to an authorization check based solely on "who you are (username)" and "where you are connecting from (host)". This removes the most critical security barrier, allowing any attacker with network access to gain entry to the database simply by guessing or knowing the username.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.fixtext: Database administrators can use the following statement to set a password for a password-less account: SET PASSWORD FOR u0 = PASSWORD('auth_string');

Rule.title: Disable creating accounts via the GRANT statement
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>When using the GRANT statement, if the target user does not exist, the system will attempt to create the user. This may lead to unintentional creation of a user with an empty password when the GRANT statement contains errors, introducing account management risks. Enabling the NO_AUTO_CREATE_USER setting in the sql_mode configuration option can prevent the GRANT statement from creating users.
Rationale: Allowing the GRANT statement to automatically create users is an implicit behavior that poses significant security risks in production environments. For example, if an administrator misspells a username during privilege assignment, the system will automatically create a new user — potentially with no password or using default settings — resulting in unintended privilege grants that could be exploited maliciously. Additionally, auto-created users may bypass organizational account provisioning processes and audit mechanisms, violating compliance requirements. Enabling the NO_AUTO_CREATE_USER mode enforces explicit user creation beforehand, improving control and security in user account management.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.fixtext: Use an administrator account with SUPER privilege to execute the following SQL: SET @@global.sql_mode=CONCAT(@@global.sql_mode, ',NO_AUTO_CREATE_USER');

Rule.title: Ensure Password Complexity Policies are in Place
Rule.description:
OceanBase MySQL tenants support configuring password complexity policies through tenant-level system variables. Enabling password complexity policies helps prevent weak password usage and raises the bar for password cracking. Variable Name Function Checks whether a user's password can be the same as the username.
- on: validate_password_check_user_name Password cannot be the same as the username.
- off: Password can be the same as the username. validate_password_length Sets the minimum length for user passwords. Sets the minimum number of uppercase and validate_password_mixed_case_count lowercase letters that the password must contain. Sets the minimum number of digits that the validate_password_number_count password must contain. Sets the password complexity policy.
- low: Only checks password length.
- medium: Checks password length, validate_password_policy uppercase letters, lowercase letters, digits, special characters, and whether the password is the same as the username. Sets the minimum number of special validate_password_special_char_count characters that the password must contain. Rationale: Complex passwords help defend against dictionary attacks, brute-force cracking, and other types of password-based attacks. This recommendation prevents users from choosing weak, easily guessable passwords, significantly enhancing account security. By enforcing a strong password policy that requires a combination of character types (uppercase, lowercase, digits, and special characters), the risk of unauthorized access is effectively reduced.

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

check.check-content: Use the following SQL statements to view the current password complexity configuration for the tenant: SHOW VARIABLES LIKE "validate_password%"; The result set should show settings that meet or exceed the following recommended baseline: • validate_password_length is 14 or more • validate_password_check_user_name is ON • validate_password_policy is MEDIUM • validate_password_mixed_case_count is 1 or more • validate_password_number_count is 1 or more • validate_password_special_char_count is 1 or more This recommendation is satisfied if the returned values meet or exceed the baseline above. This recommendation is not satisfied if any returned value does not meet the baseline.

Rule.title: Do Not Reuse Usernames
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Each database user account should be assigned a unique purpose (e.g., dedicated to a specific individual or application) and should not be shared among multiple different applications or users.
Rationale: Sharing accounts expands the scope of security risks. Once a shared account is compromised, all applications and services using that account will be exposed to threats.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

check.check-content: This recommendation requires a manual review to map database accounts to real-world owners (applications or individuals) and to confirm that accounts are not shared. 1. Obtain a list of non-reserved (non-system) users: SELECT User, Host FROM mysql.user WHERE User NOT IN ('root','ORAAUDITOR','proxyro'); 2. For each returned account, review with the DBA team, system architects, and application owners to determine: • the account owner (application/service name or individual), • the business purpose of the account, • whether the same username is used by more than one application or person. The recommendation is satisfied if each non-reserved account has a single documented owner and purpose and is not used by multiple applications or users.

Rule.title: Configure account locking after consecutive authentication failures
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>OceanBase MySQL tenants support using the tenant-level configuration parameter connection_control_failed_connections_threshold to specify the threshold for failed login attempts. Accounts exceeding this threshold will be locked, and the lock duration can be set via the parameters connection_control_min_connection_delay and connection_control_max_connection_delay. This helps prevent brute-force attacks on account passwords and enhances database security.
Rationale: Brute-force attacks and automated password guessing are common database intrusion methods, where attackers use scripts to repeatedly attempt common password combinations to gain access to legitimate accounts. Enabling a login failure attempt limit significantly increases the difficulty and time cost of such attacks, disrupting automated attack processes. By setting appropriate failure thresholds and connection delay strategies, password brute-force attempts can be effectively prevented without impacting normal user operations.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

check.check-content: Execute the following statement to review the current tenant parameter configuration: SHOW PARAMETERS LIKE 'connection_control%'; This recommendation is satisfied if the result set shows that connection_control_failed_connections_threshold is not 0 and the configured values for connection_control_min_connection_delay and connection_control_max_connection_delay meet organizational policy. This recommendation is not satisfied if connection_control_failed_connections_threshold is 0, or if the threshold and delay values do not meet organizational policy.

Rule.title: Set 'default_password_lifetime' to Require a Yearly Password Change
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>The system parameter default_password_lifetime can be used to configure the global password expiration period for OceanBase tenant users. After a password expires, it must be reset before any further operations can be performed. Configuring a password expiration period enhances operational security and system compliance, reducing the risks associated with password leakage.
Rationale: The default_password_lifetime global variable prevents passwords from being set to never expire. Overly frequent password expiration imposes more harm than benefit, as it encourages users to choose predictable passwords, such as sequential words or numbers that are easily guessed. More importantly, when a security incident occurs that may compromise passwords, account passwords should be expired immediately. It is recommended to set the password expiration period to 365 days.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

check.check-content: Execute the following SQL statement to determine the configured password expiration period: SELECT @@default_password_lifetime; This recommendation is satisfied if the returned value is set to the approved standard (for example, 365) and is not 0. This recommendation is not satisfied if the returned value is 0 (passwords never expire) or does not match the approved standard.

Rule.title: Ensure No Users Have Wildcard Hostnames
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>All user accounts in the database should be strictly restricted to connect only from specific hosts or IP addresses explicitly required for their business operations.
Rationale: The core rationale for this recommendation is the principle of least privilege and defense in depth at the network level. 1. Limit attack sources: If a user's credentials (password) are compromised, but the account is restricted to connect only from a specific application server IP, an attacker who obtains the password still cannot access the database from unauthorized locations. 2. Reduce attack surface: If a user is configured as 'user'@'%', attackers can attempt connections to the database from any location. Restricting the host/IP range significantly reduces the potential avenues for attack.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.fixtext: For each user found in the audit step using the '%' host, immediate remediation should be performed. Use the RENAME USER command (or ALTER USER, depending on the specific operation) to change the user's host from '%' to the specific IP or hostname identified in the previous step. RENAME USER 'app_user'@'%' TO 'app_user'@'10.1.2.3';

check.check-content: Execute the following SQL query to identify accounts that are allowed to connect from any host: SELECT user, host FROM mysql.user WHERE host = '%'; No rows will be returned if no accounts are configured with a wildcard host ('%'). If one or more rows are returned, at least one account allows connections from any host, and this recommendation is not satisfied.

Rule.title: Ensure 'CREATE USER' is Not Granted to Non- Administrative Users
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>The "CREATE USER" privilege controls the ability of a specific user to add or delete users, modify existing usernames, and revoke permissions from existing users.
Rationale: Reducing the number of users granted the "CREATE USER" privilege minimizes the number of users who can add or delete users, modify existing usernames, and control permissions of existing users.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.fixtext: Use the REVOKE command to revoke the CREATE USER privilege from a regular user: REVOKE CREATE USER ON *.* FROM '<user>';

check.check-content: Use the following command to view non-root users with CREATE USER privilege: SELECT * FROM information_schema.user_privileges WHERE GRANTEE NOT LIKE ("'root'%") AND PRIVILEGE_TYPE = "CREATE USER"\G No rows will be returned if no non-administrative users have the CREATE USER privilege. If one or more rows are returned, at least one non-administrative user has the CREATE USER privilege, and this recommendation is not satisfied.

Rule.title: Ensure 'PROCESS' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>The "PROCESS" privilege controls whether a specified user can view the statement execution information of all sessions.
Rationale: The "PROCESS" privilege allows a user to view the statements currently being executed by other users, even beyond their own privileges (including password management statements). Attackers may exploit this privilege to obtain potentially sensitive data or achieve privilege escalation.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.fixtext: Use the REVOKE command to remove the PROCESS privilege from a regular user: REVOKE PROCESS ON *.* FROM '<user>';

check.check-content: Use the following command to view non-root users with the PROCESS privilege: SELECT * FROM information_schema.user_privileges WHERE GRANTEE NOT LIKE ("'root'%") AND PRIVILEGE_TYPE = "PROCESS"\G No rows will be returned if no non-administrative users have the PROCESS privilege. If one or more rows are returned, at least one non-administrative user has the PROCESS privilege, and this recommendation is not satisfied.

Rule.title: Ensure 'SUPER' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>The SUPER privilege determines whether a user can perform certain powerful administrative functions, including terminating user sessions via the KILL command, modifying global MySQL variables using SET GLOBAL, and executing various commands related to replication and logging.
Rationale: The SUPER privilege determines whether a user can perform certain powerful administrative functions and should not be granted lightly. Restricting the number of accounts with the "SUPER" privilege reduces the risk of attackers exploiting these capabilities.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.fixtext: Use the REVOKE command to remove the SUPER privilege from a regular user: REVOKE SUPER ON *.* FROM '<user>';

check.check-content: Use the following command to view non-root users with the SUPER privilege: SELECT * FROM information_schema.user_privileges WHERE GRANTEE NOT LIKE ("'root'%") AND PRIVILEGE_TYPE = "SUPER"\G No rows will be returned if no non-administrative users have the PROCESS privilege. If one or more rows are returned, at least one non-administrative user has the PROCESS privilege, and this recommendation is not satisfied.

Rule.title: Use TDE for At-Rest Data Encryption
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>OceanBase supports table-granularity transparent encryption to achieve secure data storage.
Rationale: Static data is one of the key protection targets for database security. In scenarios where physical storage is at risk — such as when hard drives are discarded without proper destruction, backup media is leaked, or shared storage in cloud environments is accessed without authorization — unencrypted data can be directly read, leading to severe data breaches. Enabling TDE (Transparent Data Encryption) ensures that even if attackers obtain the underlying data files, they cannot decipher their contents.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

check.check-content: For OceanBase MySQL tenants, use the following statement: SHOW PARAMETERS LIKE 'tde_method'; If no rows are returned, this recommendation is not satisfied. This recommendation is satisfied if the returned value for tde_method is not none (for example, internal or bkmi) on all OBServer nodes. This recommendation is not satisfied if the returned value for tde_method is none on any OBServer node.

Rule.title: Ensure AES Encryption Mode is Configured Correctly
Rule.description: <VulnDiscussion>When using AES_ENCRYPT() and AES_DECRYPT() functions for encryption, it is recommended to use block cipher encryption in Cipher Block Chaining (CBC) mode with a 256-bit key length.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

check.check-content: Use the following command to check whether the current configuration parameter block_encryption_mode is set to the default value aes-128-ecb: SELECT @@GLOBAL.block_encryption_mode; This recommendation is satisfied if the returned value is aes-256-cbc (or another organizationally approved strong mode). This recommendation is not satisfied if the returned value is a weak/unapproved mode (for example, aes-128-ecb) or does not meet the approved standard.

Rule.title: Ensure ALL Events are Audited
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>The database audit function must record all critical operations to support security incident traceability, compliance reviews, and behavioral analysis.
Rationale: When comprehensive auditing is not enabled, attackers may perform covert operations (e.g., data theft, privilege escalation) through legitimate accounts and remain undetected due to lack of log evidence, making incident tracing impossible.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.title: Ensure Audit Filters Capture Connection Attempts
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>The functions audit_log_filter_set_filter and audit_log_filter_set_user are used to define audit rules, which can audit both successful and failed connection events and write them to the audit log file.
Rationale: The audit_log_filter_set_filter function is used to define audit filter rules, and the audit_log_filter_set_user function specifies which users these filter rules apply to. By creating one or more filters, audit log entries can be generated to record events for successful or failed connections.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.title: Ensure 'FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS' Is Less than or Equal to '5'
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>The FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS setting determines how many failed login attempts are permitted before the system locks the user's account. While different profiles can have different and more restrictive settings, such as USERS, the minimum(s) recommended here should be set on the DEFAULT profile.
Rationale: Repeated failed login attempts can indicate the initiation of a brute-force login attack, this value should be set according to the needs of the organization.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.fixtext: Remediate this setting by executing the following SQL statement for each PROFILE returned by the audit procedure. ALTER PROFILE <profile_name> LIMIT FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS 5;

check.check-content: To assess this recommendation, execute the following SQL statement. SELECT PROFILE,RESOURCE_NAME,LIMIT FROM SYS.DBA_PROFILES where PROFILE='DEFAULT' and RESOURCE_NAME='FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS'; When the value of FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS is too high, this recommendation is not met.

Rule.title: Ensure 'PASSWORD_LOCK_TIME' Is Greater than or Equal to '1'
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>The PASSWORD_LOCK_TIME setting determines how many days must pass for the user's account to be unlocked after the set number of failed login attempts has occurred. The suggested value for this is one day or greater.
Rationale: Locking the user account after repeated failed login attempts can block further brute- force login attacks, but can create administrative headaches as this account unlocking process always requires DBA intervention.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.fixtext: Remediate this setting by executing the following SQL statement for each PROFILE returned by the audit procedure. ALTER PROFILE <profile_name> LIMIT PASSWORD_LOCK_TIME 1;

check.check-content: To assess this recommendation, execute the following SQL statement. SELECT PROFILE,RESOURCE_NAME,LIMIT FROM SYS.DBA_PROFILES where PROFILE='DEFAULT' and RESOURCE_NAME='PASSWORD_LOCK_TIME'; The return should be 1 or greater.

Rule.title: Ensure 'PASSWORD_LIFE_TIME' Is LESS than or Equal to '365'
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>The PASSWORD_LIFE_TIME setting determines how long a password may be used before the user is required to be change it. The suggested value for this is 365 days or less.
Rationale: Allowing passwords to remain unchanged for long periods makes the success of brute- force login attacks more likely.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.fixtext: Remediate this setting by executing the following SQL statement for each PROFILE returned by the audit procedure. ALTER PROFILE <profile_name> LIMIT PASSWORD_LIFE_TIME 365;

check.check-content: To assess this recommendation, execute the following SQL statement. SELECT PROFILE,RESOURCE_NAME,LIMIT FROM SYS.DBA_PROFILES where PROFILE='DEFAULT' and RESOURCE_NAME='PASSWORD_LIFE_TIME'; The return should be 365 or less.

Rule.title: Ensure 'PASSWORD_GRACE_TIME' Is LESS than or Equal to '5'
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>The PASSWORD_GRACE_TIME setting determines how many days can pass after the user's password expires before the user's login capability is automatically locked out. The suggested value for this is five days or less.
Rationale: Locking the user account after the expiration of the password change requirement's grace period can help prevent password-based attacks against any forgotten or disused accounts, while still allowing the account and its information to be accessible by DBA intervention.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.fixtext: Remediate this setting by executing the following SQL statement for each PROFILE returned by the audit procedure. ALTER PROFILE <profile_name> LIMIT PASSWORD_GRACE_TIME 5;

check.check-content: To assess this recommendation, execute the following SQL statement. SELECT PROFILE,RESOURCE_NAME,LIMIT FROM SYS.DBA_PROFILES where PROFILE='DEFAULT' and RESOURCE_NAME='PASSWORD_GRACE_TIME'; The return should be 5 or less.

Rule.title: Ensure 'PASSWORD_VERIFY_FUNCTION' Is Set for All Profiles
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>The PASSWORD_VERIFY_FUNCTION determines password settings requirements when a user password is changed at the SQL command prompt. It should be set for all profiles.
Rationale: Through database profiles, password complexity rules (mixed cases with digits and special characters), blocking of simple combinations, and enforcing change/history settings can potentially thwart unauthorized logins by an unauthorized user.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

check.check-content: To assess this recommendation, execute the following SQL statement. SELECT PROFILE,RESOURCE_NAME,LIMIT FROM SYS.DBA_PROFILES where RESOURCE_NAME='PASSWORD_VERIFY_FUNCTION'; The query result should not show NULL. Instead, it should return a valid password verification function name.

Rule.title: Ensure Passwords are Set for All Accounts
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Blank passwords allow a user to login without using a password.
Rationale: Without a password only knowing the username will allow someone to connect to the server and assume the identity of the user. This, in effect, bypasses authentication mechanisms.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.fixtext: For each user from the audit procedure which password is NULL, reset the password for the given user using the following statement. ALTER USER <username> IDENTIFIED BY <password>;

Rule.title: Public Role Privileges
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>The unnecessary privileges should be revoked from default public role to minimize security risks and adhere to the principle of least privilege.
Rationale: The privileges must be structured to block unauthorized use and/or corruption of vital data and services by setting restrictions on user capabilities, particularly those of the role PUBLIC. Such security measures help to ensure successful logins cannot be easily redirected.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.title: Minimum Privileges
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>The unnecessary privileges should be revoked from user to minimize security risks and adhere to the principle of least privilege.
Rationale: The privileges must be structured to block unauthorized use and/or corruption of vital data and services by setting restrictions on user capabilities. Minimum privilege security measures help to ensure successful logins cannot be easily redirected.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.title: Only Allowed Client can Access to Cluster
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Specify an client whitelist of approved servers that can access to the cluster.
Rationale: When using clients by specifying the allowlist explicitly, it can increase the security of the cluster as only servers in the allowlist are allowed to connect to the cluster.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.fixtext: Remediate this setting by executing the following SQL statement: SET GLOBAL ob_tcp_invited_nodes='<all_ip_list>';

Rule.title: Use TDE for At-Rest Data Encryption
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) at-rest encryption protects your critical data by enabling data-at-rest encryption in the database. It protects the privacy of your information, prevents data breaches and helps meet regulatory requirements.
Rationale: File system based encryption does a good job of protecting against data theft on devices unable to limit physical access. It does not, however, protect against users who have or gain access to the operating system, backups, over the network copies, etc. Encrypting data from database adds an additional layer of data protection.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.title: Ensure 'AUDIT_TRAIL' is not set to NONE
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>The audit_trail setting determines whether or not OceanBase's basic audit features are enabled. It can be set to OS (Operating System); DB; DB_EXTENDED; or DB, EXTENDED. The value should be set according to the needs of the organization. NONE means audit is disabled.
Rationale: Enabling the basic auditing features for the OceanBase permits the collection of data to troubleshoot problems, as well as provides valuable forensic logs in the case of a system breach this value should be set according to the needs of the organization.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

check.check-content: To assess this recommendation, execute the following SQL statement. SELECT svr_ip,name,value FROM oceanbase.GV$OB_PARAMETERS WHERE name='audit_trail'; The return should be OS or DB or DB_EXTENDED or DB,EXTENDED.

Rule.title: Ensure 'AUDIT_SYS_OPERATIONS' is set to TRUE
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>The AUDIT_SYS_OPERATIONS setting provides for the auditing of all user activities conducted under the SYS accounts. The setting should be set to TRUE to enable this auditing.
Rationale: If the parameter AUDIT_SYS_OPERATIONS is FALSE, all statements by SYS users are not audited.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark

Rule.fixtext: To remediate this setting, execute one of the following SQL statements. ALTER SYSTEM SET AUDIT_SYS_OPERATIONS = TRUE;

check.check-content: To assess this recommendation, execute the following SQL statement. SELECT svr_ip,name,value FROM oceanbase.GV$OB_PARAMETERS WHERE name='audit_sys_operations'; The return should be TRUE.

Rule.title: Enable Audit Options According to Requirements
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Enabling the audit option causes auditing of any attempt, successful or not to do database operations. For auditing requests, audit rule should be configured to align with specific requirements.
Rationale: Logging of all database operations can provide forensic evidence about a pattern of suspect/unauthorized activities. Any unauthorized attempt may be cause for further investigation.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS OceanBase Enterprise Edition V4 Benchmark
